evidence.title: Beyond VLAs: How World Action Models Reshape Robot Manipulation
evidence.excerpt: Robotics English 中文 Beyond VLAs: How World Action Models Reshape Robot Manipulation Aug 04, 2026 By Saeed Babamohamadi Discuss (0) L T F R E AI-Generated Summary World action models (WAMs) replace vision-language model backbones with video world models to give robot policies a physics prior for predicting how scenes evolve. NVIDIA research shows WAMs learn from diverse interaction data, generalize to unseen environments through learned dynamics, and adapt to new robot embodiments with fewer demonstrations than vision-language-action models. NVIDIA Cosmos 3 provides an open omni-model foundation trained on 767 million images, 348 million real-world dynamics videos, and 8 million action samples spanning manipulation, driving, and egocentric motion. Cosmos 3 Policy DROID models post-trained from the 16B Nano and 4B Edge checkpoints jointly predict action trajectories and future camera views while retaining the full multimodal architecture. Deployment options include workstation serving with the 16B Nano model on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 and on-device inference with the 4B Edge model on Jetson Thor at 15 Hz control frequency.
